definitions.explanation: The act of changing from one thing to another, such as switching systems, modes, or approaches.
Shifting one's mental focus or attitude, especially recovering from a setback.

examples.japanese: システムの{切|き}り{替|か}えは{深夜|しんや}に{行|おこな}う。
examples.english: The system switchover will be done late at night.

examples.japanese: {気持|きも}ちの{切|き}り{替|か}えが{大事|だいじ}だ。
{夏時間|なつじかん}への{切|き}り{替|か}えが{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: The changeover to daylight saving time was implemented.

notes:
WORD STRUCTURE:
{切|き}り{替|か}える (to switch) → {切|き}り{替|か}え (noun form)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{切|き}り{替|か}えを{行|おこな}う - to carry out a switchover
・{気持|きも}ちの{切|き}り{替|か}え - mental shift
・{画面|がめん}{切|き}り{替|か}え - screen switching
・{季節|きせつ}の{切|き}り{替|か}え - seasonal change

IT/TECHNICAL USES:
・システム{切|き}り{替|か}え - system switchover
・{切|き}り{替|か}えスイッチ - toggle switch
・{入力|にゅうりょく}{切|き}り{替|か}え - input switching
・{言語|げんご}{切|き}り{替|か}え - language switching

SPORTS/PSYCHOLOGY:
{切|き}り{替|か}え is important in sports and business - the ability to mentally recover from mistakes and refocus.
・{失敗|しっぱい}を{引|ひ}きずらずに{切|き}り{替|か}える - to not dwell on failure and move on
